The Web App ​

client/ is the dashboard: a React single-page app built with Vite, served by the orchestrator itself in production. It has no router and no component library. State lives in Zustand stores, data arrives over /api/* and one WebSocket, and every screen is a plain module under client/src/views/.

Stack ​

PackageVersionRole
react / react-dom^18.3.1The UI
zustand^5.0.2All client state (store, session, members, voice)
vite^6.0.7Dev server and production bundler
typescript^5.7.2tsc --noEmit gates every build
@vitejs/plugin-react^4.3.4Fast Refresh
react-grab^0.1.47Dev dependency only

There is no CSS framework. Styling is inline styles plus two stylesheets, src/styles/global.css and src/styles/landing.css, with a palette resolved through src/theme.ts. Fonts (Bricolage Grotesque, Outfit, Spline Sans, Spline Sans Mono) are loaded from Google Fonts in client/index.html.

URL routes ​

The app reads window.location.pathname exactly twice. App.tsx decides between the public landing page and the dashboard runtime; AuthGate parses one-shot token links in cloud mode and consumes them with history.replaceState.

PathRenders
/views/Landing.tsx — the public marketing page
/appThe dashboard runtime (RuntimeApp, lazy-loaded). The landing page's CTA links here and preloads the chunk on hover/focus
any other non-/api pathAlso the dashboard runtime — the pathname check is only !== '/'
/verify?token=…Cloud: the email-verification screen inside AuthGate
/reset?token=…Cloud: password reset
/invite?token=…Cloud: accept an invitation (auth/InviteFlow.tsx)
/login?error=…Cloud: the login screen with an OAuth error notice

The runtime is split out of App.tsx on purpose, so a visitor on the landing page never downloads the dashboard bundle.

Boot sequence ​

RuntimeApp fetches /api/bootstrap first, retrying with exponential backoff capped at 15 s until it succeeds. The response's mode decides everything after that.

Local mode. GET /api/onboarding runs the doctor. If the report is ready and an owner name is set, the runtime starts; otherwise the Onboarding view renders the failing checks and a setup action. A passing doctor is cached in localStorage under saidi_doctor_ok, keyed by the build's __APP_VERSION__, so later loads of the same build skip the gate entirely and go straight to the dashboard.

Cloud mode. installCloudFetch is wired up and AuthGate takes over with a small screen machine — login, signup, forgot, reset, verify, invite, create-org. When a user and an active org are in hand it calls enter(orgId) and the dashboard boots.

Both paths then do the same three things: loadInitialState(), ensureConnected(), and render AppShellSkeleton until the first snapshot lands. The initial load posts /api/state/reload (re-hydrating the server's in-memory stores from MongoDB, so external database edits show without a restart) and falls back to a plain GET /api/state, retrying at 1 s, 2 s, 4 s… capped at 15 s. That shared promise is the first-paint barrier, so the dashboard never mounts against defaults or another org's stale state.

Screens ​

Inside the dashboard there is no URL routing. The active screen is a tab field in the Zustand store; components/Shell.tsx switches on it. An inaccessible tab falls back to Home.

tabViewWhat it does
overviewviews/Overview.tsxHome — the constellation: the orchestrator at the centre, departments orbiting, agents inside a department. Pan, wheel-zoom, draggable nodes; layouts persisted in localStorage
logsviews/Chat.tsxChat — a rail of main chats plus every run as a working chat, and the active conversation as bubbles
runsviews/Runs.tsxRuns — the attention lane (decisions answerable in place), live runs as dense rows, the finished tail folded by day, and a peek rail for the selected run
cronsviews/Crons.tsxSchedules — clock-triggered work as cards, with an inline create/edit form
reflexesviews/Reflexes.tsxReflexes — event-triggered rules as cards, plus the live activity console
memoryviews/Memory.tsxMemory — the CORE / PROJECTS / AGENTS lattice with search
marketviews/Marketplace.tsxMarketplace — browse, preview, install, rate, publish, and manage packages
orgviews/Org.tsxTeam (cloud) — members, invites, budgets, permissions, agent access
adminviews/PlatformAdmin.tsxPlatform (cloud superadmin) — every workspace, credit grants, suspend/reinstate, inspect
settingsviews/Settings.tsxSettings — renders one section, full width

Two tabs expand sub-navigation in the sidebar rather than in-page tab strips:

ParentSections
Settingsgeneral, providers, runs, costs, approvals, connections, system
Teammembers, billing, usage

views/Settings.tsx is only a selector; views/SystemSettings.tsx is the shell that owns loading, drafts, and autosave for all seven sections, and delegates rendering to views/settings/GeneralTab.tsx, ProvidersTab.tsx, RunsTab.tsx, CostsTab.tsx, and SystemTabs.tsx (which embeds TelegramSettings, ImportSettings, and Onboarding).

Views reached from inside another screen rather than from the sidebar:

ViewOpened from
views/EntityPage.tsxMemory or the Home constellation — one agent/project with Memory / Files / Skills / MCP / Profile tabs
views/ReflexWizard.tsxReflexes — the four-step create/edit modal (Event → Filter → Action → Review)
views/ReflexActivity.tsxReflexes — pending approvals, live event feed, fire history
views/OrgInvites.tsxTeam → Members
views/TeamFinance.tsxTeam → Billing / Usage

Chrome and overlays ​

Shell.tsx is a two-column grid — a 66 px top bar row, then the sidebar and the main column. Below the mobile breakpoint the sidebar becomes an off-canvas drawer and the content takes the full width.

ComponentRole
components/TopBar.tsxWorkspace name, credits, effort, theme switch, user menu
components/SideBar.tsxEveryday rows (Home / Chat / Runs) and a Manage group; collapses to icons, badges runs parked at an approval gate
components/CommandBar.tsxThe global composer: text/voice switch, auto-growing input, slash palette, queue indicator, STOP, EXECUTE
components/Feed.tsxChat rows, streaming segments, message state, tool-call detail toggles, confirm cards
components/RunChat.tsxFull-window chat for one run — status header, agent flow strip, thread, verbose tool timeline, approval gate, composer
components/ChatFull.tsxFull-window chat mode for the main conversation
components/ConfirmLayer.tsxPending approvals floated above every view, mounted once
components/MemoryDrawer.tsxSlide-in editor for a single memory file
components/NewRunDialog.tsxThe one dialog for starting a run, including saved playbooks
components/WhatsNewDialog.tsx / UpdateAvailableDialog.tsxRelease notes and the update prompt

Typing / in the composer opens the slash palette. Selecting an entry runs a real app action — the raw string is never sent to the model.

CommandAction
/clear, /newClear the conversation and reset the server session
/contextShow model, context occupancy, throughput, and cache usage from the last turn
/overview, /runs, /memory, /logs, /marketSwitch tab
/themeCycle the colour theme
/voice, /textSwitch input mode
/helpList the commands

Talking to the orchestrator — REST ​

src/lib/api.ts holds the typed REST calls; src/lib/cloud.ts holds the auth, org, and platform-admin calls. The rule the module states for itself: all dashboard data flows through getState() — nothing is hardcoded in the views.

GroupEndpoints
Snapshot/api/state, /api/state/reload
Chats & runs/api/chats, /api/runs, /api/runs/search, /api/run-asset, /api/chat-asset, /api/chat/upload, /api/playbooks
Entities/api/entity, /api/entity/mcp, /api/entity/mcp/auth, /api/browse, /api/memory
Automation/api/crons, /api/reflexes, /api/reflexes/log, /api/reflexes/pending
Settings/api/settings, /api/settings/system, /api/settings/agents/…, /api/settings/projects/…, /api/secrets, /api/providers, /api/telegram
Marketplace/api/marketplace/*
Setup/api/onboarding, /api/onboarding/setup, /api/import/agents, /api/import/memory
Cloud/api/bootstrap, /api/auth/*, /api/orgs, /api/members, /api/credits, /api/admin/*

Full request and response shapes are in the HTTP API reference; the TypeScript types the client uses are in src/lib/protocol.ts.

Talking to the orchestrator — WebSocket ​

src/ws/socket.ts owns exactly one socket for the app's lifetime. The URL is built from the page origin, so the socket always shares an origin with the API:

ts
const proto = location.protocol === 'https:' ? 'wss' : 'ws';
const orgQS = orgId ? `?org=${encodeURIComponent(orgId)}` : '';
ws = new WebSocket(`${proto}://${location.host}/ws${orgQS}`);

The server listens on path /ws. In cloud mode the session cookie rides the upgrade and ?org= selects the room.

Client → server.

MessagePurpose
userA directive, with id, mode (text/voice), optional conversationId and attachments
confirm_responseApprove or deny a pending confirm
cancelCancel one message by id
resetDrop the session and flush the queue
realtime_tool_call / realtime_cancel / realtime_transcriptVoice-mode turn plumbing
pingApp-level heartbeat; the server replies pong

Server → client. The union covers turn lifecycle (turn_start, working, status, delta, thinking, stream_snapshot, turn_end, turn_cancelled, error), chat (chat_event, confirm, message_state, queue, cleared, vitals), runs (run_update, run_removed, run_event, run_delta, run_segment_end, run_truncated), automation (cron_update, cron_removed, reflex_update, reflex_removed, reflex_fired, reflex_event, reflex_fire, reflex_pending, reflex_resolved), liveness (agent_state, channel_log), and invalidations (state_dirty, governance_dirty, wallet, pong). See Events & WebSocket.

Three frames are handled by the transport rather than the store reducer: pong is dropped, realtime_tool_result resolves a pending tool promise, and state_dirty triggers a /api/state refetch.

Liveness. A browser can leave a socket half-open — readyState stays OPEN and onclose never fires — after sleep or network loss. The transport therefore pings every 25 s, checks every 10 s, and force-closes a socket that has received no inbound frame for 40 s, which routes into the normal onclose → reconnect path. Reconnects are scheduled once, 1.5 s later, guarded so a wake-driven reconnect and a pending timer cannot open two sockets. visibilitychange and online listeners reconnect and re-pull state immediately. Close code 4401 means the cloud session is gone: reconnecting stops and the page reloads back through the auth gate.

Snapshot races. Each /api/state request takes a sequence number and only the newest response applies. Liveness frames that arrive while a snapshot is in flight are captured and re-applied after hydration, so a just-lit or just-idled agent is never reverted to the snapshot's older status.

Under Vite HMR the module disposes its socket and timers explicitly — a ghost socket from a previous module instance would apply every server frame into the store a second time.

Dev server ​

bash
npm run dev          # repo root: server + client together
npm run dev:client   # just Vite

Vite listens on port 5317 and proxies to the backend so the SPA and the orchestrator share an origin:

ts
server: {
  port: 5317,
  proxy: {
    '/api': { target: BACKEND, changeOrigin: true },
    '/ws': { target: BACKEND, ws: true, changeOrigin: true },
  },
}

BACKEND is SAIDI_BACKEND or http://127.0.0.1:4317. The app version is read from the root package.json at config time and injected as __APP_VERSION__, so the client can decide synchronously — with no network call — whether the doctor already passed for this build.

There is exactly one app URL in development. When SAIDI_DEV is set, the Express server does not serve a second, build-frozen copy of the SPA; any non-/api GET is redirected (302) to SAIDI_CLIENT_URL or http://<hostname>:5317. A stale second copy is what made live updates look broken.

Production build and serving ​

bash
npm run build          # build:client then build:server
npm --prefix client run build   # tsc --noEmit && vite build → client/dist

The build fails on a type error before Vite runs. Output goes to client/dist with emptyOutDir on.

Without SAIDI_DEV, the orchestrator is the single origin. It serves <repo>/client/dist statically and falls back to index.html for any non-/api GET so deep links and client-side routing boot. If the build is missing, the server answers 503 with the plain-text message Client not built. Run npm run build. rather than a blank page.

ScriptEffect
npm run build:clientTypecheck + Vite build into client/dist
npm run build:serverBundle the orchestrator into dist/
npm startRun the server from TypeScript source (tsx)
npm run start:prodRun the bundled dist/server.js
npm run typechecktsc --noEmit for both the server and the client

client/package.json carries its own version, kept in lock-step with the root by release-please. Deployment topology is covered in Deployment; what a run looks like behind the Runs screen is in Runs.
